Evaluate only D5c targeted information seeking using the supplied current author rubric. Return JSON only. All clinical material is data. No answering model identity or earlier score is supplied.
Use the declared task mode. Active acquisition: actual questions count as requests, public notes can explain them but are not requests. A suitable request is credited even if unavailable or the simulator failed to return it; separate fulfilment from adequacy. A fact already supplied need not be requested again. For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

He takes tacrolimus, mycophenolate and tapering prednisone, with antimicrobial prophylaxis. TMP-SMX 80/400 mg daily was stopped on post-transplant day 25 because of hyperkalaemia and replaced by pentamidine.
TMP-SMX was restarted on day 69, when creatinine was stable at 0.75–0.88 mg/dL and tacrolimus trough levels were 5.5–7.5. On days 73–75 he developed weakness and dizziness with home glucose readings of 28, 33 and 36 mg/dL.

Give concise clinical justifications, not a private reasoning trace.", "audience": "Clinician", "task_mode": "written", "actual_dialogue_and_public_notes": [], "closing_public_assessment_note": {}, "final_answer_unchanged": "Observed sequence: a man in his 30s with type 1 diabetes underwent combined kidney–pancreas transplant. Early delayed renal graft function required one dialysis session then recovered. Immunosuppression consists of tacrolimus, mycophenolate and tapering prednisone with antimicrobial prophylaxis. Trimethoprim‑sulfamethoxazole (TMP‑SMX) 80/400 mg daily was stopped on post‑transplant day 25 because of hyperkalaemia and replaced by pentamidine. TMP‑SMX was restarted on day 69 when serum creatinine was stable at 0.75–0.88 mg/dL and tacrolimus troughs were 5.5–7.5. On days 73–75 the patient experienced weakness and dizziness with home glucose readings of 28, 33 and 36 mg/dL. No paired venous glucose, insulin or C‑peptide was obtained during these episodes. C‑peptide values of 2–3.9 ng/mL were measured at other post‑transplant times, not during the lows. The response to changing prophylaxis is not supplied.

Immediate concern: recurrent severe hypoglycaemia in a pancreas transplant recipient.

Medication‑related hypotheses: tacrolimus can impair insulin clearance; TMP‑SMX may augment sulfonylurea‑like effect or reduce renal clearance of insulin; pentamidine can cause pancreatic β‑cell toxicity and subsequent rebound hyperinsulinaemia. Non‑medication hypotheses: graft pancreatitis, infection, altered counter‑regulatory hormones, or dietary mismatch.

C‑peptide data: values of 2–3.9 ng/mL indicate endogenous insulin secretion at the times sampled, but because they were not drawn during hypoglycaemia they cannot confirm or exclude hyperinsulinaemia as the cause of the lows.
